# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_07f98c80cd

Run `run_09c0dd1caca0` · blinded · 2026-10-31 19:34 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e2 | 1 | 1 | 201 | act_std z=+139.0; tub_glcm_contrast z=+138.7; act_glcm_contrast z=+104.4 |
| e3 | 10 | 1 | 112 | tub_glcm_contrast z=+185.2; act_std z=+179.3; act_glcm_contrast z=+138.0 |
| e7 | 3 | 1 | 200 | act_std z=+168.7; tub_glcm_contrast z=+140.0; act_glcm_contrast z=+119.3 |
| e8 | 0.3 | 1 | 346 | act_std z=+66.9; act_glcm_contrast z=+50.3; tub_glcm_contrast z=+38.5 |

## Steps

1. `list_available_experiments` — Need to see doses and replicates to plan discriminative well acquisitions.

3. `acquire_well` — Sample highest dose to reveal maximal phenotype for MoA discrimination.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Eg5 inhibitors 0.50, Microtubule destabilizers 0.25, Actin disruptors 0.10, Microtubule stabilizers 0.10, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05
- after step 12: Eg5 inhibitors 0.55, Microtubule destabilizers 0.20, Microtubule stabilizers 0.10, Actin disruptors 0.10, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05

## Conclusion

**Eg5 inhibitors** (stated probability 0.55); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e9, e10.

Why: NSC is 2-2 tie with low similarity; dose-dependent mitotic arrest plus microscopist monopolar morphology favor Eg5 over actin.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution spindle-polarity imaging with tubulin plus centrosome marker to test monopolar versus bipolar arrest, with phospho-H3 mitotic index and washout recovery, compared to a reference of the leading class.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean on drug-class biology, no drug property issues.

## Unblinding

Compound: **cytochalasin D** (PubChem CID [5458428](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5458428))

Identity check: name only (the BBBC021 structure is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Actin disruptors**, BBBC021 annotates **Actin disruptors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (2/4). The Scientist's own call was **Eg5 inhibitors** (dissents; wrong).

## Reflection

My scientist call of Eg5 inhibitors (p=0.55) was wrong; the protocol 1-NN majority was right with Actin disruptors 2/4 votes winning on summed similarity 1.225 vs 1.174 for Eg5. The actin signal was present from the start: act_std z=+139 to +179 and act_glcm_contrast z=+104 to +138 in e2/e3/e7, and the low-dose well w_b617e84d8d at 0.3 uM was already nearest Actin disruptors at similarity 0.63, the single highest similarity in the run.

I was misled by the dose-dependent frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 in e10 and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 in e11 plus the microscopist candidates of Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers/Eg5 inhibitors in e4, which I read as monopolar arrest favoring Eg5. I over-weighted the second compare_to_reference_atlas k-neighbour count of Eg5 6/10 in e9 and treated the 2-2 NSC tie as favoring Eg5, while ignoring that all similarities were low at 0.575-0.63 and that strong actin texture changes support direct actin perturbation consistent with PMID 3023337 and PMID 40658853.

The acquisition choice hurt: I sampled only four mid-high doses from 0.3 to 10 uM and described only 2 fields, without testing lower-dose onset, replicates, or an actin-specific readout to resolve rounding-induced mitotic-like morphology from true spindle arrest. Actin depolymerization and secondary cell rounding can inflate tubulin contrast and mitotic-like features, so texture alone could not separate the classes.

What was right:
- Acquired wells showed extreme actin features act_std z up to +179.3 and act_glcm_contrast up to +138.0 alongside tubulin changes, consistent with actin disruption
- Final NSC vote was 2-2 tie with Actin disruptors winning on summed similarity 1.225 vs 1.174, and the 0.3 uM well nearest Actin at 0.63 was the strongest match
- K-neighbour lists retained Actin disruptors 2/10 then 3/10, keeping the true class alive despite Eg5 majority

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-interpreted dose_response frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 and tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 as Eg5-specific mitotic arrest rather than secondary rounding/mitotic-like morphology from actin loss
- Accepted describe_phenotype candidates of Eg5/microtubule agents and discounted Actin disruptors, although e4 listed only microtubule/Eg5 options
- Treated low NSC similarities 0.575-0.63 and Eg5 6/10 k-neighbour plurality as decisive for Eg5 instead of uncertain, and stopped after 4 high/mid-dose wells without low-dose or replicate acquisitions to test stability

Proposed next experiment: Fixed-cell counter-screen with phalloidin for F-actin plus tubulin/pericentrin for spindle polarity across 0.03-10 uM, comparing the unknown to cytochalasin D and an Eg5 inhibitor control, quantifying cortical actin loss, cell rounding/multinucleation, bipolar vs monopolar spindles, and phospho-H3 mitotic index with washout recovery.

## Citations

Citations verified: 4/4

- PMID [3023337](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3023337/): Actin polymerization. The mechanism of action of cytochalasin D. *J Biol Chem* (1986) — Cytochalasin D blocks actin polymerization by capping filament barbed ends.
- PMID [40658853](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40658853/): Microscopic and structural observations of actin filament capping and severing by cytochalasin D. *Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A* (2025) — Structural and microscopic work shows cytochalasin D caps and severs actin filaments.
- PMID [3782101](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3782101/): The kinetics of cytochalasin D binding to monomeric actin. *J Biol Chem* (1986) — Cytochalasin D binds monomeric actin with defined kinetics.
- PMID [22728040](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22728040/): Cytochalasin D acts as an inhibitor of the actin-cofilin interaction. *Biochem Biophys Res Commun* (2012) — Cytochalasin D also inhibits the actin-cofilin interaction.

Cost: $0.3310 over 14 model calls; 12 Scientist turns.
